facts: Santiago is a young Andalusian shepherd who beds his flock down in an abandoned church; a sycamore grows through the roof of the old sacristy.
In his dream a child takes him by the hands, leads him to the Egyptian pyramids and says that if he goes there he will find a hidden treasure.
Just before the child shows the exact spot, Santiago wakes. The same dream comes a second time in the same place and ends the same way.
In Tarifa a gypsy woman interprets the dream as an instruction to go to the pyramids and asks a tenth of the treasure for the reading.
An old man who turns out to be the King of Salem tells him about a Personal Legend, the thing a person has always wanted to accomplish, and that most people stop believing it is possible.
Santiago sells his sheep and crosses to Africa.
On his first day in Tangier a young man who offers to guide him leaves him with no money. He is in a foreign port with the pyramids still far away.
scene_details: A sycamore growing through the roof of an abandoned church's sacristy
A child leading him by the hands toward the pyramids and the dream breaking off before the spot is shown
Sheep sold and a port town where his money disappears on day one
tension: A shepherd has the same unfinished dream twice and has to decide what a dream is worth when the cost is the flock that makes his living.
opening_idea: Start in the ruined church under the sycamore, with the sleeping shepherd and the dream that stops one step before the answer.

lessons.idea: A wish that returns unchanged is worth testing with a real, affordable step instead of being argued about forever.
lessons.anchor: The dream came twice, identical and incomplete, and Santiago acted on it by selling the sheep and crossing to Africa.
lessons.everyday_example_idea: A cook who keeps imagining her own small place books one weekend stall at a market.

reflect_final: Which idea keeps coming back to you, in more or less the same form, and what small step could you take toward it this month?

use_cases.situation: A friend keeps describing the same plan and never starts it.
use_cases.move: Santiago's dream arrived twice before he moved. Ask the friend what the smallest real step would be, and when.

use_cases.situation: You have an idea you keep postponing.
use_cases.move: Write the idea in one sentence and the first step that costs little, then choose a day for it.

use_cases.situation: A family member is afraid of giving up a safe job.
use_cases.move: Santiago sold the flock to go; ask what part of the safe thing they would keep and what part they could test first.

pocket_idea: A dream that comes back unchanged is asking for a first step, the way Santiago's twice-dreamed pyramids sent him to sell his sheep.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: Santiago's dream stopped one step short of the answer, twice, and he sold his sheep anyway.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Shepherd sleeps in a ruined church, dreams of a child leading him to the pyramids, wakes before the spot is shown. Dreams it again. A gypsy woman reads it as go, an old king talks about a Personal Legend, and he sells the flock. First day in Tangier he is robbed.
